content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: IVR outage message plus 20% chat deflection for payment-status and refund calls, with payments breaks delayed 45 min. Predicted 88.6% service level for 12:45-14:45 at ₹1,116.","why":"The spike is caused by the IMPS/NEFT payment hub incident (INC-20261023-2029). Customers are calling about pending transfers and refunds: payment_status_enquiry is up 66 calls and refund_status up 53. Staffing and attendance are at plan. Doing nothing leaves the window at 58.8%, with payments at 48.5% and 9.3% abandons. P2 tells callers about the known issue and moves some of them to chat. That lifts the window to 88.6% (payments 88.2%, general 89.1%) and cuts abandons to 2.0%. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that clears the 80% target. Rest of day is predicted at 92.9%.","trade_offs":["P1 (no cost: delay breaks + callback) reaches only 66.6%, well short of the 80% target, with payments at 60.9% and 6.9% abandons.","P4 (15 overtime agents + outage message + callback) gives a similar 88.3% at nearly double the cost (₹2,160). The general queue would sit lower, at 86.3% versus 89.1%.","P3 (25 overtime agents) reaches 96.9% and 0.4% abandons, but costs ₹5,976, more than five times P2, for margin beyond the target.","P2 protects the general queue (89.1%) as well as payments. It does depend on customers accepting the outage message and chat deflection."],"watch":"Watch payments volume and service level in the 13:00-13:30 intervals. If the incident escalates or deflection uptake is weak and service level stays below 80%, consider adding overtime (P4 or P3). Watch for an incident resolution update so the IVR message can be removed promptly."}
